newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar down but not out against mark in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Dollar down but not out against mark in Singapore.

text.p: The U.S. dollar fell against the mark on Monday as the German currency was bought up against the yen and European crosses amid continuing speculation Germany would raise interest rates, Singapore dealers said.
There was also talk of stop-loss sales being triggered in dollar/mark.
"We were caught by surprise. We thought 1.81 was a good level where people would buy the dollar, but someone just pushed the trigger," a European bank dealer said.
He said the 1.7980-1.8050 marks region now represented a key support band for the dollar.
"If this breaks, I think the uptrend would be broken for a while. Otherwise we're still in a consolidation with maybe a delay in the uptrend," he said.
Dealers said the market was not expecting the U.S. Federal Reserve to hike short-term rates at its policy-setting meeting on Tuesday.
"Nobody's expecting anything from the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee meeting) tomorrow. And for Germany, it makes no sense to raise rates," the dealer said.
He said the dollar would face a barrier around 1.8255 marks.
The German central bank is expected to set the securities repurchase agreements (repo) rate on Tuesday and will hold a council meeting on Thursday after a four-week summer break.
